title: Revelation 16 — The seven bowls: Har-magedon + the great earthquake and hail

translation.sourceText: Koine Greek New Testament — SBL Greek New Testament (SBLGNT), ed. Michael W. Holmes (Society of Biblical Literature and Logos Bible Software, 2010), printed text with the variant-marker sigla removed. Primary uncial witnesses for Revelation: Codex Sinaiticus (א/01) and Codex Alexandrinus (A/02), with Ephraemi Rescriptus (C/04) and P47/P115 where extant; Codex Vaticanus (B/03) does not contain Revelation in its original hand. Variants against NA28 and the Byzantine/Textus Receptus tradition are reported in the verse commentary (overlay convention sblgnt-base-text-variant-reporting-convention-revelation).

verdicts.reasoning: ēkousa megalēs phōnēs ek tou naou legousēs ... Hypagete kai ekcheete tas hepta phialas tou thymou tou theou eis tēn gēn. Exact.
apēlthen ho prōtos kai execheen tēn phialēn autou eis tēn gēn; egeneto helkos kakon kai ponēron. 'foul and grievous sore' (ASV). Exact.

pasa psychē zōēs apethanen ta en tē thalassē: line changed from ASV 'every living soul' to 'every living being'. psychē zōēs reproduces nep̄eš ḥayyâ of sea creatures; 'soul' would import a personal sense. Defensible and governed by the overlay psychē entry. Non-blocking: the SBLGNT marks a variant at zōēs (TR zōsa, KJV 'every living soul'); the note could name it.
exechee ... eis tous potamous kai tas pēgas tōn hydatōn; kai egeneto haima. Exact.

citations: Bauckham, The Theology of the Book of Revelation (1993)
Metzger, A Textual Commentary on the Greek New Testament (2nd ed. 1994), on Rev 16:5
verdicts.reasoning: Dikaios ei, ho ōn kai ho ēn, ho hosios: the two-membered divine-name formula without 'who is to come'; ho hosios as vocative title 'O Holy One'. The TR 'and shalt be' from Beza's conjecture is a well-documented secondary reading. Defensible and accurately reported.
haima hagiōn kai prophētōn exechean, kai haima autois dedōkas piein; axioi eisin. 'They are worthy of it' with 'of it' supplied and flagged. Exact.

citations: SBLGNT (no variant marker: Robinson-Pierpont also reads tou thysiastēriou)
verdicts.reasoning: ēkousa tou thysiastēriou legontos: 'I heard the altar saying'; TR allou ek correctly attributed to the TR. Nai, kyrie, ho theos, ho pantokratōr matches 4:8 ('Lord God the Almighty'). Exact.
execheen tēn phialēn autou epi ton hēlion; edothē autō kaumatisai tous anthrōpous en pyri. autō = the sun, noted. Exact.

tou echontos tēn exousian epi tas plēgas tautas: line changed from ASV 'the power' to 'authority'. exousia epi + accusative is jurisdiction, rendered 'authority over' at 6:8 (published) and 13:7, so the change is grammatically motivated and consistent. Defensible; governed by the overlay exousia entry.
exechee ... epi ton thronon tou thēriou; egeneto hē basileia autou eskotōmenē, kai emasōnto tas glōssas autōn ek tou ponou. Exact.
eblasphēmēsan ton theon tou ouranou ek tōn ponōn autōn kai ek tōn helkōn autōn. Exact.
epi ton potamon ton megan ton Euphratēn; exēranthē to hydōr autou, hina hetoimasthē hē hodos tōn basileōn tōn apo anatolēs hēliou. Exact.
ek tou stomatos tou drakontos ... pneumata tria akatharta hōs batrachoi. 'coming out of' supplied for the elliptical ek-phrases. Exact.
eisin gar pneumata daimoniōn poiounta sēmeia ... eis ton polemon tēs hēmeras tēs megalēs tou theou tou pantokratoros. Exact.
Idou erchomai hōs kleptēs. makarios ho grēgorōn ...: unattributed speech in quotation marks, consistent with the program convention and the SBLGNT dashes; noted. Exact.
synēgagen (sg. with neuter plural pneumata) autous eis ton topon ton kaloumenon Hebraisti Harmagedōn: 'they gathered', 'Har-magedon' (ASV) keeps har without deciding the etymology. Defensible.
exechee ... epi ton aera; exēlthen phōnē megalē ek tou naou apo tou thronou legousa: Gegonen. Exact.

citations: SBLGNT (variant marker on anthrōpoi egenonto and on phōnai kai brontai)
KJV Rev 16:18 ('voices, and thunders, and lightnings ... since men were upon the earth')
verdicts.reasoning: English line approved: astrapai kai phōnai kai brontai ... aph' hou anthrōpoi egenonto epi tēs gēs ... tēlikoutos seismos houtō megas is exactly rendered. Commentary fix: the note says the Textus Receptus has the singular; the TR and KJV have the plural ('since men were'), and the singular anthrōpos egeneto is the reading NA28 prints (with Alexandrinus) against the SBLGNT's plural, so the NA28 divergence the overlay convention requires is unreported and the TR attribution is inverted. Proposed: 'The SBLGNT reads the plural anthrōpoi egenonto; NA28 prints the singular anthrōpos egeneto; the Textus Receptus has the plural (KJV since men were upon the earth). The sense is the same.' Also name the TR order 'voices, and thunders, and lightnings', which the canon's English edition quotes. The reviewer's NA28 wording is from recollection: check it against the printed NA28 before applying. Reception note verified; no leakage.
egeneto hē polis hē megalē eis tria merē ... Babylōn hē megalē emnēsthē enōpion tou theou dounai autē to potērion tou oinou tou thymou tēs orgēs autou. 'fury of his wrath' keeps thymos/orgē. Exact.
pasa nēsos ephygen, kai orē ouch heurethēsan. Literal; reception note verified; no leakage.

chalaza megalē hōs talantiaia katabainei (present) ... eblasphēmēsan ... hoti megalē estin hē plēgē autēs sphodra. 'about a talent in weight' without the ASV's supplied 'every stone' is closer to the Greek. Reception note (FR 'lingots', EN KJV wording) verified; no leakage.

citations: SBLGNT (Holmes 2010) variant markers at Rev 16:18 and 21:3, and their absence at 8:7, 10:4, 12:17, 16:7, 21:2
Metzger, A Textual Commentary on the Greek New Testament (2nd ed. 1994)
glossaryReview.reasoning: claim_type direct is right: the entry declares which text is translated and how variants are reported. Three accuracy fixes. (1) The 8:7 omission is a Textus Receptus (minority) reading, not that of the Byzantine majority text, which the SBLGNT apparatus shows agreeing with SBLGNT; rephrase wherever 'Byzantine' is said there. (2) Add 21:3 'out of heaven' (TR ek tou ouranou, quoted by the canon's English) to the wohChoice list of KJV-wording variants, and 16:18 (NA28 singular anthrōpos egeneto; TR order 'voices, thunders, lightnings'). (3) Add REV-WOH-16:18's NA28 divergence to the 'NA28 bracketed or divergent readings reported' sentence. The decision itself stands.

citations: LXX usage: kyrios for the Tetragrammaton, theos for ʾĕlōhîm
glossaryReview.reasoning: Direct is correct: theos never renders the Tetragrammaton in the LXX or NT, the canon's French reads 'Dieu' at every site, and published chapters 1, 4, 6 use 'God'. The canon's English 'Yahweh'/'Elohim' is recorded in reception notes without entering the line.

citations: BDAG s.vv. diabolos, Satanas, Abaddōn, Harmagedōn
glossaryReview.reasoning: Direct is correct for a presentation and scope convention. Recommendation (non-blocking): state the scope criterion explicitly. Hebrew-text central entries are applied to a Greek line when their English choice is also a correct rendering of the Greek lexeme (chayyot 'living creatures' at 7:11; gophrit 'sulfur' for theion). They are background only where applying them would import a Hebrew-specific form or sense (Yisra'el, 'the adversary', 'the deep'). Without that sentence the 7:11 chayyot ref and the gophrit extension look like exceptions to rule (4).

Direct is defensible: BDAG separates the capability and jurisdiction senses, Revelation sets dynamis beside exousia at 13:2, and exousia epi + accusative is uniformly 'authority over' (6:8, 13:7, 16:9). The 16:9 line change follows the construction, not the lens.

Direct is defensible: at 8:9 and 16:3 the psychai are sea creatures, and psychē zōēs reproduces nep̄eš ḥayyâ. 'every living being' matches RSV/NRSV in sense. Non-blocking: the 16:3 TR variant zōsa (KJV 'every living soul') could be named in the rationale.

citations: Bauckham, The Theology of the Book of Revelation (1993)

reviewerReport.lensLeakageCheck: Every English line was checked: all 146 lines, and specifically the 21 reception-note sites (7:3, 8:1, 8:7, 8:8, 8:10, 8:12, 9:1, 9:5, 9:9, 9:13, 9:18, 10:4, 10:7, 12:12, 13:18, 16:18, 16:20, 16:21, 21:1, 21:2, 21:3). A script found no Elohim, Yahweh, YHWH, craft, missile, atomic, nuclear, planet, Eternals, loudspeaker or similar lens vocabulary in any line. The only hits were 'ship(s)' (8:9 ploia; worship) and 'Israel' (substring 'rael'), both benign. Each Wheel of Heaven reading sits in its own headed paragraph labelled 'reception note, not a translation claim'. Each was verified against LWTE ch. 2 (LWTE-2:155-228), FR and EN. No line resolves an ambiguity in the canon's direction: the visionary hōs/homoios markers are kept (8:8; 9:7-10), 'the number of a man' stays open (13:18), 'breastplates' is used rather than the canon's French 'thorax' (9:9), 'pit of the abyss' is kept (9:1), and theos is 'God' where the canon's English has 'Yahweh'/'Elohim' (9:13; 21:2-4). Where the line and the canon's English diverge, the line follows the Greek critical text, and at 8:7 that text agrees with the canon's French.
reviewerReport.escalationReportAdjustments: Initial verdicts on all 146 verses, the 10 overlay entries touched and the 13 diff ops were formed from the chapters, the SBLGNT sources (including the sigla-bearing Rev.txt in the scratchpad), the overlay, the diff and the 2.80.0 base before opening wave-r2-editor-report.md. After reading the report, no verdict changed. The report's Founder point C lists the KJV-wording variants named in commentary (8:7, 9:13, 10:4, 21:2, 21:3 'his people ... their God', 21:4). It omits 21:3 'out of heaven', which confirms the reviewer's 21:3 revise. Its 9:13 request ('the Reviewer should verify this against the NA28 apparatus') was met as far as possible: the SBLGNT marker confirms a collated edition reads tessarōn, and the corrected attribution agrees with the reviewer's reading of Metzger. The printed NA28 apparatus was not available, so this is recorded as unverified at the sigla level, not as a defect. The report's 'All other lines are the Translator's draft, unchanged' was confirmed by diffing against the rev_r2 backup: only 16:3 and 16:9 differ.

founderDecisionRecommendations.A-theion-sulfur: Endorse. LXX theion = gophrit (Gen 19:24), BDAG 'sulfur', NRSV 'sulfur' at all four sites; the central entry already renders the Revelation lake passages 'sulfur'. The canon's English 'brimstone' (9:18) is recorded.
founderDecisionRecommendations.B-theos-God-not-Yahweh-Elohim: Endorse firmly. theos does not render the Tetragrammaton, the canon's own French has 'Dieu', and chapters 1, 4, 6 are signed off with 'God'. Writing 'Yahweh' would translate the canon's English edition, not the Greek.
founderDecisionRecommendations.C-critical-text-over-KJV-wording: Endorse. Complete the inventory: add 21:3 'out of heaven' (TR ek tou ouranou) and 16:18 (NA28 singular; TR order 'voices, thunders, lightnings'); correct 8:7 to say the omission is a TR reading, not the Byzantine majority's. Optionally name 16:3 zōsa and 21:4 hoti.
founderDecisionRecommendations.D-names-and-scope-rule: Endorse, and support promotion to a central Greek-NT convention. Add the explicit criterion (apply where the central English is also a correct rendering of the Greek lexeme; background where it imports a Hebrew-specific form), which explains chayyot at 7:11 and gophrit for theion.
founderDecisionRecommendations.E-exousia: Endorse. The context rule follows BDAG's sense division and RSV/NRSV practice; 16:9 'authority over' aligns with 6:8 and 13:7. Uniform 'authority' would read badly at 9:10, 19.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F-16:3-living-being: Endorse. 'soul' for sea creatures imports a personal sense; 'living being' keeps the noun and the nep̄eš ḥayyâ echo.
founderDecisionRecommendations.G-doulos-servants: Endorse. Keeps the signed-off 1:1/6:11 and the canon's English 'servants'; the French 'esclaves' is recorded.
founderDecisionRecommendations.H-pit-of-the-abyss: Endorse. ASV structure; matches the canon's French 'le puits de l'abîme'.
founderDecisionRecommendations.I-Har-magedon: Endorse. ASV form, follows the SBLGNT/NA28 rough breathing, keeps har visible without deciding the etymology.
founderDecisionRecommendations.J-12:18-versification: Endorse. P47, Sinaiticus and Alexandrinus read estathē, and SBLGNT/NA28 number it 12:18 (Metzger on 12:18). The ASV 13:1a alignment is a tooling task (orchestrator follow-up 2), not a translation issue.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ἤκουσα μεγάλης φωνῆς ἐκ τοῦ ναοῦ λεγούσης τοῖς ἑπτὰ ἀγγέλοις· Ὑπάγετε καὶ ἐκχέετε τὰς ἑπτὰ φιάλας τοῦ θυμοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ εἰς τὴν γῆν.
paragraphs.translit: kai ēkousa megalēs phōnēs ek tou naou legousēs tois hepta angelois· hypagete kai ekcheete tas hepta phialas tou thymou tou theou eis tēn gēn.

i18n.en: And I heard a loud voice out of the temple saying to the seven angels: "Go and pour out the seven bowls of the wrath of God onto the earth."

notes.official: *megalēs phōnēs ek tou naou* 'a loud voice out of the temple': the voice is God's own, since no one could enter the temple until the plagues were finished (15:8). *phialas* 'bowls' are the shallow cultic bowls of the sanctuary (Ex 27:3; Zech 14:20), here filled with God's *thymos* 'wrath'. The seven bowls follow the order of the trumpets (earth, sea, rivers, sun, darkness, Euphrates, air) and the plagues of Egypt, now without the limiting 'third'. *ekcheete* 'pour out': Ps 69:24; Jer 10:25; Zeph 3:8.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ἀπῆλθεν ὁ πρῶτος καὶ ἐξέχεεν τὴν φιάλην αὐτοῦ εἰς τὴν γῆν· καὶ ἐγένετο ἕλκος κακὸν καὶ πονηρὸν ἐπὶ τοὺς ἀνθρώπους τοὺς ἔχοντας τὸ χάραγμα τοῦ θηρίου καὶ τοὺς προσκυνοῦντας τῇ εἰκόνι αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai apēlthen ho prōtos kai execheen tēn phialēn autou eis tēn gēn· kai egeneto helkos kakon kai ponēron epi tous anthrōpous tous echontas to charagma tou thēriou kai tous proskynountas tē eikoni autou.

i18n.en: And the first went and poured out his bowl onto the earth; and a foul and grievous sore came upon the people who had the mark of the beast and who worshiped its image.

notes.official: *helkos kakon kai ponēron* 'a foul and grievous sore': the sixth Egyptian plague (Ex 9:9-11, *helkē* LXX) and the covenant curse of Deut 28:27, 35, 'the boil of Egypt'. *to charagma tou thēriou* 'the mark of the beast' (13:16).

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ὁ δεύτερος ἐξέχεεν τὴν φιάλην αὐτοῦ εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν· καὶ ἐγένετο αἷμα ὡς νεκροῦ, καὶ πᾶσα ψυχὴ ζωῆς ἀπέθανεν τὰ ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ.
paragraphs.translit: kai ho deuteros execheen tēn phialēn autou eis tēn thalassan· kai egeneto haima hōs nekrou, kai pasa psychē zōēs apethanen ta en tē thalassē.

i18n.en: And the second poured out his bowl into the sea; and it became blood like that of a dead man, and every living being died, the things that were in the sea.

notes.official: *haima hōs nekrou* 'blood like that of a dead man': congealed blood. *pasa psychē zōēs apethanen* 'every living being died': *psychē zōēs* reproduces the *nep̄eš ḥayyâ* of Gen 1:20-21, 24, the 'living creatures' with which the waters swarm (LXX *psychē zōsa*). The line follows that sense and replaces the ASV/KJV 'every living soul' (`psyche-soul-life-living-being-rendering-revelation`; cf. the central `nefesh-chayah` 'living being', background); RSV and NRSV have 'every living thing'. The Textus Receptus reads *psychē zōsa* 'living soul' for *psychē zōēs* (KJV 'every living soul'). *ta en tē thalassē* 'the things that were in the sea' stands in apposition (ASV 'even the things that were in the sea'). Cf. 8:8-9 and Ex 7:20-21.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ὁ τρίτος ἐξέχεεν τὴν φιάλην αὐτοῦ εἰς τοὺς ποταμοὺς καὶ τὰς πηγὰς τῶν ὑδάτων· καὶ ἐγένετο αἷμα.
paragraphs.translit: kai ho tritos execheen tēn phialēn autou eis tous potamous kai tas pēgas tōn hydatōn· kai egeneto haima.

i18n.en: And the third poured out his bowl into the rivers and the springs of the waters; and it became blood.

notes.official: The first Egyptian plague (Ex 7:17-21), extended to rivers and springs as at the third trumpet (8:10).

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἤκουσα τοῦ ἀγγέλου τῶν ὑδάτων λέγοντος· Δίκαιος εἶ, ὁ ὢν καὶ ὁ ἦν, ὁ ὅσιος, ὅτι ταῦτα ἔκρινας,
paragraphs.translit: kai ēkousa tou angelou tōn hydatōn legontos· dikaios ei, ho ōn kai ho ēn, ho hosios, hoti tauta ekrinas,

i18n.en: And I heard the angel of the waters saying: "Righteous are you, who are and who were, O Holy One, because you have judged these things;

notes.official: *tou angelou tōn hydatōn* 'the angel of the waters': angels set over the elements (7:1; 14:18; 1 En 66:2; Jub 2:2). *Dikaios ei, ho ōn kai ho ēn, ho hosios* 'Righteous are you, who are and who were, O Holy One': the divine-name formula of 1:4, 8 and 4:8 (`apo-ho-on-rev-1-4-solecism-preservation-convention`; central `apo-ho-on-rev-1-4-greek-grammatical-solecism-divine-name-cross-corpus` and `ehyeh-asher-ehyeh-divine-name-revelation-ex-3-14-cross-corpus`) without its third member. 'Who is to come' is dropped because the coming is now taking place (cf. 11:17; Bauckham, *The Theology of the Book of Revelation*, 1993, 29). The Textus Receptus reads 'which art, and wast, and shalt be' (KJV), from Beza's conjecture *ho esomenos* in place of *ho hosios*, which no Greek manuscript supports (Metzger, *Textual Commentary*², ad loc.). The line follows the SBLGNT (`sblgnt-base-text-variant-reporting-convention-revelation`). *ho hosios* 'O Holy One': cf. Deut 32:4 LXX, 'righteous and holy is the Lord'. *hoti tauta ekrinas* 'because you have judged these things'.

paragraphs.text: ὅτι αἷμα ἁγίων καὶ προφητῶν ἐξέχεαν, καὶ αἷμα αὐτοῖς δέδωκας πιεῖν· ἄξιοί εἰσιν.
paragraphs.translit: hoti haima hagiōn kai prophētōn exechean, kai haima autois dedōkas piein· axioi eisin.

i18n.en: for they poured out the blood of saints and prophets, and you have given them blood to drink. They are worthy of it."

notes.official: *haima hagiōn kai prophētōn exechean* 'they poured out the blood of saints and prophets' (Ps 79:3). *kai haima autois dedōkas piein* 'and you have given them blood to drink' (Isa 49:26). *axioi eisin* 'They are worthy of it', i.e. deserving; the punishment matches the crime. 'Of it' is supplied (ASV 'they are worthy').

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἤκουσα τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου λέγοντος· Ναί, κύριε, ὁ θεός, ὁ παντοκράτωρ, ἀληθιναὶ καὶ δίκαιαι αἱ κρίσεις σου.
paragraphs.translit: kai ēkousa tou thysiastēriou legontos· nai, kyrie, ho theos, ho pantokratōr, alēthinai kai dikaiai hai kriseis sou.

i18n.en: And I heard the altar saying: "Yes, O Lord God the Almighty, true and righteous are your judgments."

notes.official: *ēkousa tou thysiastēriou legontos* 'I heard the altar saying' is the reading of the SBLGNT and NA28; the Textus Receptus reads *allou ek tou thysiastēriou* 'another out of the altar' (KJV). The line follows the SBLGNT (`sblgnt-base-text-variant-reporting-convention-revelation`). The altar that speaks is the one under which the martyrs cried 'How long?' (6:9-10) and on which the prayers were offered (8:3-5), and it now answers that cry. *Nai, kyrie, ho theos, ho pantokratōr* 'Yes, O Lord God the Almighty' (4:8; 15:3). *alēthinai kai dikaiai hai kriseis sou* 'true and righteous are your judgments': Ps 19:9; 119:137.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ὁ τέταρτος ἐξέχεεν τὴν φιάλην αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὸν ἥλιον· καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ καυματίσαι τοὺς ἀνθρώπους ἐν πυρί.
paragraphs.translit: kai ho tetartos execheen tēn phialēn autou epi ton hēlion· kai edothē autō kaumatisai tous anthrōpous en pyri.

i18n.en: And the fourth poured out his bowl upon the sun; and it was given to it to scorch people with fire.

notes.official: *execheen tēn phialēn autou epi ton hēlion* 'poured out his bowl upon the sun'. *edothē autō kaumatisai tous anthrōpous en pyri* 'it was given to it to scorch people with fire': *autō* refers to the sun (ASV 'it was given unto it').

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἐκαυματίσθησαν οἱ ἄνθρωποι καῦμα μέγα· καὶ ἐβλασφήμησαν τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ἔχοντος τὴν ἐξουσίαν ἐπὶ τὰς πληγὰς ταύτας, καὶ οὐ μετενόησαν δοῦναι αὐτῷ δόξαν.
paragraphs.translit: kai ekaumatisthēsan hoi anthrōpoi kauma mega· kai eblasphēmēsan to onoma tou theou tou echontos tēn exousian epi tas plēgas tautas, kai ou metenoēsan dounai autō doxan.

i18n.en: And the people were scorched with great heat, and they blasphemed the name of God who has authority over these plagues, and they did not repent so as to give him glory.

notes.official: *ekaumatisthēsan hoi anthrōpoi kauma mega* 'the people were scorched with great heat' (cognate accusative). *tou echontos tēn exousian epi tas plēgas tautas* 'who has authority over these plagues': *exousia epi* with the accusative is jurisdiction 'over', as at 6:8 ('authority ... over a quarter of the earth') and 13:7 ('authority over every tribe'). The line therefore changes the draft's 'the power' (ASV) to 'authority', in line with those sites (`exousia-authority-power-rendering-revelation`). *ou metenoēsan dounai autō doxan* 'they did not repent so as to give him glory' (cf. 11:13; 14:7).

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ὁ πέμπτος ἐξέχεεν τὴν φιάλην αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὸν θρόνον τοῦ θηρίου· καὶ ἐγένετο ἡ βασιλεία αὐτοῦ ἐσκοτωμένη, καὶ ἐμασῶντο τὰς γλώσσας αὐτῶν ἐκ τοῦ πόνου,
paragraphs.translit: kai ho pemptos execheen tēn phialēn autou epi ton thronon tou thēriou· kai egeneto hē basileia autou eskotōmenē, kai emasōnto tas glōssas autōn ek tou ponou,

i18n.en: And the fifth poured out his bowl upon the throne of the beast; and its kingdom was darkened, and they gnawed their tongues because of the pain,

notes.official: *epi ton thronon tou thēriou* 'upon the throne of the beast' (13:2). *egeneto hē basileia autou eskotōmenē* 'its kingdom was darkened': the ninth Egyptian plague (Ex 10:21-23). *emasōnto tas glōssas autōn* 'they gnawed their tongues': the imperfect implies repeated action.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἐβλασφήμησαν τὸν θεὸν τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἐκ τῶν πόνων αὐτῶν καὶ ἐκ τῶν ἑλκῶν αὐτῶν, καὶ οὐ μετενόησαν ἐκ τῶν ἔργων αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: kai eblasphēmēsan ton theon tou ouranou ek tōn ponōn autōn kai ek tōn helkōn autōn, kai ou metenoēsan ek tōn ergōn autōn.

i18n.en: and they blasphemed the God of heaven because of their pains and their sores, and they did not repent of their works.

notes.official: *ton theon tou ouranou* 'the God of heaven': the title of Dan 2:18-19, 37, 44 and of Ezra-Nehemiah, in Revelation only here and at 11:13. *ek tōn ponōn autōn kai ek tōn helkōn autōn* 'because of their pains and their sores' (v 2).

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ὁ ἕκτος ἐξέχεεν τὴν φιάλην αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὸν ποταμὸν τὸν μέγαν τὸν Εὐφράτην· καὶ ἐξηράνθη τὸ ὕδωρ αὐτοῦ, ἵνα ἑτοιμασθῇ ἡ ὁδὸς τῶν βασιλέων τῶν ἀπὸ ἀνατολῆς ἡλίου.
paragraphs.translit: kai ho hektos execheen tēn phialēn autou epi ton potamon ton megan ton euphratēn· kai exēranthē to hydōr autou, hina hetoimasthē hē hodos tōn basileōn tōn apo anatolēs hēliou.

i18n.en: And the sixth poured out his bowl upon the great river, the Euphrates; and its water was dried up, so that the way might be prepared for the kings from the rising of the sun.

notes.official: *ton potamon ton megan ton Euphratēn* 'the great river, the Euphrates' (9:14). *exēranthē to hydōr autou* 'its water was dried up': the drying of the sea and the Jordan (Ex 14:21; Josh 3:16-17) and of the Euphrates in the oracles against Babylon (Isa 11:15; 44:27; Jer 50:38; 51:36); Cyrus took Babylon by diverting the river (Herodotus 1.191). *tōn basileōn tōn apo anatolēs hēliou* 'the kings from the rising of the sun', i.e. from the east (7:2); in the first century, the Parthians.

paragraphs.text: καὶ εἶδον ἐκ τοῦ στόματος τοῦ δράκοντος καὶ ἐκ τοῦ στόματος τοῦ θηρίου καὶ ἐκ τοῦ στόματος τοῦ ψευδοπροφήτου πνεύματα τρία ἀκάθαρτα ὡς βάτραχοι·
paragraphs.translit: kai eidon ek tou stomatos tou drakontos kai ek tou stomatos tou thēriou kai ek tou stomatos tou pseudoprophētou pneumata tria akatharta hōs batrachoi·

i18n.en: And I saw, coming out of the mouth of the dragon and out of the mouth of the beast and out of the mouth of the false prophet, three unclean spirits like frogs;

notes.official: *pneumata tria akatharta hōs batrachoi* 'three unclean spirits like frogs': the second Egyptian plague (Ex 8:1-7); frogs are unclean animals (Lev 11:10, 41). *tou pseudoprophētou* 'the false prophet', named here for the first time, is the second beast of 13:11-17. *pneuma* is 'spirit' here (cf. 13:15).

paragraphs.text: εἰσὶν γὰρ πνεύματα δαιμονίων ποιοῦντα σημεῖα, ἃ ἐκπορεύεται ἐπὶ τοὺς βασιλεῖς τῆς οἰκουμένης ὅλης, συναγαγεῖν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸν πόλεμον τῆς ἡμέρας τῆς μεγάλης τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ παντοκράτορος—
paragraphs.translit: eisin gar pneumata daimoniōn poiounta sēmeia, ha ekporeuetai epi tous basileis tēs oikoumenēs holēs, synagagein autous eis ton polemon tēs hēmeras tēs megalēs tou theou tou pantokratoros—

i18n.en: for they are spirits of demons, performing signs, which go out to the kings of the whole world, to gather them for the war of the great day of God the Almighty.

notes.official: *pneumata daimoniōn poiounta sēmeia* 'spirits of demons, performing signs' (cf. 13:13-14). *tēs oikoumenēs holēs* 'of the whole world' (cf. 12:9). *eis ton polemon tēs hēmeras tēs megalēs tou theou tou pantokratoros* 'for the war of the great day of God the Almighty': the day of YHWH (Joel 2:11; Zeph 1:14). The SBLGNT closes the verse with a dash, marking v 15 as an interruption.

paragraphs.text: Ἰδοὺ ἔρχομαι ὡς κλέπτης. μακάριος ὁ γρηγορῶν καὶ τηρῶν τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ, ἵνα μὴ γυμνὸς περιπατῇ καὶ βλέπωσιν τὴν ἀσχημοσύνην αὐτοῦ—
paragraphs.translit: idou erchomai hōs kleptēs. makarios ho grēgorōn kai tērōn ta himatia autou, hina mē gymnos peripatē kai blepōsin tēn aschēmosynēn autou—

i18n.en: "Behold, I am coming like a thief! Blessed is the one who stays awake and keeps his garments, so that he may not walk about naked and they see his shame."

notes.official: *Idou erchomai hōs kleptēs* 'Behold, I am coming like a thief!': a saying of the risen Christ, inserted without introduction, as at 22:7; it repeats 3:3 and the saying of Matt 24:43 and 1 Thess 5:2. The SBLGNT sets it off with dashes and the ASV with parentheses; the line encloses it in quotation marks without an attribution, under the program's convention for direct speech. *makarios* 'Blessed' is the third of the book's seven beatitudes (1:3; 14:13; 16:15; 19:9; 20:6; 22:7, 14). *tērōn ta himatia autou* 'keeps his garments' (cf. 3:4, 18). *tēn aschēmosynēn autou* 'his shame', i.e. his nakedness (Ex 20:26 LXX).

paragraphs.text: καὶ συνήγαγεν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸν τόπον τὸν καλούμενον Ἑβραϊστὶ Ἁρμαγεδών.
paragraphs.translit: kai synēgagen autous eis ton topon ton kaloumenon hebraisti harmagedōn.

i18n.en: And they gathered them to the place that is called in Hebrew Har-magedon.

notes.official: *kai synēgagen autous* 'And they gathered them': the verb is singular with the neuter plural *pneumata* (v 14) as its subject, so 'they' are the spirits. *eis ton topon ton kaloumenon Hebraisti Harmagedōn* 'to the place that is called in Hebrew Har-magedon'. The name is usually explained as Heb. *har məḡiddô* 'mountain of Megiddo', after the plain where kings fought and fell (Judg 5:19; 2 Kgs 23:29-30; Zech 12:11), although no mountain bears that name; another proposal is *har môʿēd* 'the mount of assembly' (Isa 14:13) (Aune, WBC 52B; Koester, AB 38A). The ASV form 'Har-magedon' is kept: it follows the Greek with the rough breathing (SBLGNT *Harmagedōn*; Textus Receptus *Armageddōn*, KJV 'Armageddon') and shows the element *har* 'mountain' without deciding the etymology (`greek-nt-proper-names-and-hebrew-scoped-entries-convention-revelation`).

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ὁ ἕβδομος ἐξέχεεν τὴν φιάλην αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὸν ἀέρα— καὶ ἐξῆλθεν φωνὴ μεγάλη ἐκ τοῦ ναοῦ ἀπὸ τοῦ θρόνου λέγουσα· Γέγονεν—
paragraphs.translit: kai ho hebdomos execheen tēn phialēn autou epi ton aera— kai exēlthen phōnē megalē ek tou naou apo tou thronou legousa· gegonen—

i18n.en: And the seventh poured out his bowl upon the air; and a loud voice came out of the temple, from the throne, saying: "It is done!"

notes.official: *epi ton aera* 'upon the air', the last of the elements. *ek tou naou apo tou thronou* 'out of the temple, from the throne'. *Gegonen* 'It is done!' is a perfect (cf. John 19:30 *tetelestai*); the plural form returns at 21:6.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἐγένοντο ἀστραπαὶ καὶ φωναὶ καὶ βρονταί, καὶ σεισμὸς ἐγένετο μέγας, οἷος οὐκ ἐγένετο ἀφʼ οὗ ἄνθρωποι ἐγένοντο ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς τηλικοῦτος σεισμὸς οὕτω μέγας,
paragraphs.translit: kai egenonto astrapai kai phōnai kai brontai, kai seismos egeneto megas, hoios ouk egeneto aphʼ hou anthrōpoi egenonto epi tēs gēs tēlikoutos seismos houtō megas,

i18n.en: And there were lightnings and voices and thunders, and there was a great earthquake, such as had not been since people were upon the earth, so great an earthquake, so mighty.

notes.official:
*astrapai kai phōnai kai brontai* 'lightnings and voices and thunders': the theophany series (8:5) reaches its fullest form here. The Textus Receptus has the order *phōnai kai brontai kai astrapai* (KJV 'voices, and thunders, and lightnings'), which the canon's English edition quotes. *seismos ... megas, hoios ouk egeneto aph' hou anthrōpoi egenonto epi tēs gēs* 'a great earthquake, such as had not been since people were upon the earth': the formula of Dan 12:1 and Ex 9:18, 24. The SBLGNT and the Textus Receptus both read the plural *anthrōpoi egenonto* (KJV 'since men were upon the earth'); some critical editions read the singular, with the same sense (`sblgnt-base-text-variant-reporting-convention-revelation`). *tēlikoutos seismos houtō megas* 'so great an earthquake, so mighty'.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *Let's Welcome the Extra-Terrestrials* (ch. 2) quotes this verse and reads the earthquake as the shock of atomic explosions, made greater still if they set off a chain reaction. The line renders *seismos* 'earthquake' and adds nothing.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἐγένετο ἡ πόλις ἡ μεγάλη εἰς τρία μέρη, καὶ αἱ πόλεις τῶν ἐθνῶν ἔπεσαν· καὶ Βαβυλὼν ἡ μεγάλη ἐμνήσθη ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ δοῦναι αὐτῇ τὸ ποτήριον τοῦ οἴνου τοῦ θυμοῦ τῆς ὀργῆς αὐτοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: kai egeneto hē polis hē megalē eis tria merē, kai hai poleis tōn ethnōn epesan· kai babylōn hē megalē emnēsthē enōpion tou theou dounai autē to potērion tou oinou tou thymou tēs orgēs autou·

i18n.en: And the great city was split into three parts, and the cities of the nations fell. And Babylon the great was remembered before God, to give her the cup of the wine of the fury of his wrath.

notes.official: *hē polis hē megalē* 'the great city' is Babylon (cf. 17:18; 18:10). *egeneto ... eis tria merē* 'was split into three parts' (literally 'came to be in three parts'). *Babylōn hē megalē* 'Babylon the great': Dan 4:30; Rev 14:8. *emnēsthē enōpion tou theou* 'was remembered before God': remembered for judgement. *to potērion tou oinou tou thymou tēs orgēs autou* 'the cup of the wine of the fury of his wrath': the cup of Jer 25:15-29 and Isa 51:17, with *thymos* 'fury' and *orgē* 'wrath' combined.

paragraphs.text: καὶ πᾶσα νῆσος ἔφυγεν, καὶ ὄρη οὐχ εὑρέθησαν.
paragraphs.translit: kai pasa nēsos ephygen, kai orē ouch heurethēsan.

i18n.en: And every island fled away, and the mountains were not found.

notes.official:
*pasa nēsos ephygen, kai orē ouch heurethēsan* 'every island fled away, and the mountains were not found': the dissolution of the world before judgement (6:14; 20:11; cf. Ps 97:5; Isa 40:4).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *Let's Welcome the Extra-Terrestrials* (ch. 2) quotes this verse and reads it as the effect of a monstrous explosion, caused by a chain reaction, that drives the continents apart, engulfs the islands and sweeps the mountains away. The line renders the Greek literally and adds nothing.

paragraphs.text: καὶ χάλαζα μεγάλη ὡς ταλαντιαία καταβαίνει ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἐπὶ τοὺς ἀνθρώπους· καὶ ἐβλασφήμησαν οἱ ἄνθρωποι τὸν θεὸν ἐκ τῆς πληγῆς τῆς χαλάζης, ὅτι μεγάλη ἐστὶν ἡ πληγὴ αὐτῆς σφόδρα.
paragraphs.translit: kai chalaza megalē hōs talantiaia katabainei ek tou ouranou epi tous anthrōpous· kai eblasphēmēsan hoi anthrōpoi ton theon ek tēs plēgēs tēs chalazēs, hoti megalē estin hē plēgē autēs sphodra.

i18n.en: And great hail, about a talent in weight, comes down out of heaven upon the people; and the people blasphemed God because of the plague of the hail, for its plague is exceedingly great.

notes.official:
*chalaza megalē hōs talantiaia* 'great hail, about a talent in weight': *talantiaios* 'weighing a talent', roughly 25 to 40 kg depending on the standard (BDAG; Aune, WBC 52B). The ASV supplies 'every stone'; the line does not. Hail is the seventh Egyptian plague (Ex 9:23-25), and great hailstones fall on the enemies of YHWH at Josh 10:11 and Ezek 38:22. *katabainei* 'comes down' is present. *ek tēs plēgēs tēs chalazēs* 'because of the plague of the hail'.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *Let's Welcome the Extra-Terrestrials* (ch. 2) quotes this verse. Its French reads 'une grande grêle comme des lingots' ('great hail like ingots'), and its English edition 'every stone about the weight of a talent' (KJV). It reads the hail as rocks falling from the sky thousands of kilometres from the places where the bombs fell. The line renders *talantiaia* by its weight and adds nothing.
